quizzes.title: Java Programming Fundamentals
quizzes.description: Test your understanding of Java OOPs, JVM architecture, keywords, collections, and exception handling.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to inherit a class in Java?
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword is used in Java to inherit the properties and methods of a parent class into a child class.

questions.question: What is the size of an int data type in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, an 'int' is always 32 bits (4 bytes) regardless of the underlying operating system or processor architecture.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid Java access modifier?
questions.explanation: Java has public, private, and protected modifiers (and default package-private when no modifier is specified). 'friendly' is not a Java keyword.

questions.question: Which method is called automatically when an object is created?
questions.explanation: A Constructor is a special method that is invoked automatically when an instance of a class is created using the 'new' keyword.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'finally' block in Java exception handling?
options: To execute important code such as closing resources whether an exception is handled or not
To rethrow exceptions to the calling method
To terminate the Java Virtual Machine immediately
questions.explanation: The 'finally' block always executes after try/catch blocks, ensuring cleanup code (like closing streams or db connections) is guaranteed to run.

questions.question: Which collection class allows key-value pairs and does not allow duplicate keys?
questions.explanation: HashMap stores elements as key-value pairs where each key must be unique. If a duplicate key is inserted, it overrides the existing value.

questions.question: Can an abstract class have constructors in Java?
options: Yes, to initialize fields when a subclass instance is created
No, because abstract classes cannot be instantiated
Only if the constructor is declared as private
questions.explanation: Yes! Abstract classes can have constructors. They are called via super() from subclass constructors when a concrete subclass is instantiated.

questions.question: Which feature of OOP is demonstrated by having multiple methods in the same class with the same name but different parameters?
questions.explanation: Method Overloading (compile-time polymorphism) allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists within the same class.

questions.question: What does the 'static' keyword on a variable signify?
options: The variable cannot be modified once assigned
The variable belongs to the class rather than individual instances
The variable is stored on the Stack memory
The variable is only accessible from within the same package
questions.explanation: A static variable is shared among all instances of a class and belongs to the class itself rather than any individual object.

questions.question: Which of the following creates a thread in Java?
options: Extending the Thread class or implementing Runnable interface
Using the 'synchronized' keyword on a class
questions.explanation: Threads in Java are created either by extending java.lang.Thread or implementing java.lang.Runnable (or Callable with ExecutorService).

quizzes.title: General Science & Everyday Technology
quizzes.description: Explore questions on basic physics principles, chemical reactions, cell biology, and modern computing devices.

questions.question: What gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants absorb Carbon Dioxide (CO₂) and water, and use sunlight energy to synthesize glucose and release Oxygen.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for ordinary table salt?
questions.explanation: Table salt is Sodium Chloride, chemical formula NaCl.

questions.question: Which organelle is famously known as the 'Powerhouse of the Cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce the majority of cellular energy in the form of Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP).

questions.question: What is the speed of light in a vacuum approximately?
questions.explanation: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 km/s (or ~300,000 km/s / 3 × 10⁸ m/s).

questions.question: Which element is the most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen gas makes up roughly 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume.

questions.question: What type of wave is sound?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal compression wave that requires a physical medium (solid, liquid, gas) to propagate.

questions.question: What is the unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: The standard SI unit of electrical resistance is the Ohm (represented by the Greek letter Ω).

questions.question: Which component of blood is primarily responsible for transporting oxygen?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain the iron-rich protein hemoglobin, which binds oxygen molecules in the lungs and delivers them to bodily tissues.

questions.question: What is the pH level of pure, neutral water at 25°C?
questions.explanation: Pure water has a neutral pH of 7. Values below 7 are acidic, while values above 7 are basic/alkaline.

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system is known as the 'Red Planet'?
questions.explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet because iron minerals in its soil oxidize (rust), giving the surface a reddish appearance.

quizzes.title: Mathematics & Quantitative Aptitude
quizzes.description: Solve problems in arithmetic, percentages, algebraic equations, probability, and speed-time-distance.

questions.question: If a shirt marked at $80 is sold with a 25% discount, what is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Discount = 25% of $80 = 0.25 * 80 = $20. Selling Price = $80 - $20 = $60.

questions.question: What is the value of x if: 3x + 15 = 45?
questions.explanation: Subtract 15 from both sides: 3x = 30. Divide by 3: x = 10.

questions.question: What is the probability of rolling an even number on a standard fair 6-sided die?
questions.explanation: Even numbers on a die are 2, 4, 6 (3 outcomes). Total possible outcomes = 6. Probability = 3/6 = 1/2 (50%).

questions.question: A train travels at 72 km/h. How many meters does it travel in 10 seconds?
questions.explanation: Convert km/h to m/s: 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Distance in 10 seconds = 20 m/s * 10 s = 200 meters.

questions.question: What is the square root of 625?
What is the next number in the sequence: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___?
questions.explanation: Differences between terms: +4, +6, +8, +10. The next difference is +12. Thus 30 + 12 = 42 (also n*(n+1) formula: 6*7 = 42).

questions.question: If the radius of a circle is doubled, by what factor does its area increase?
questions.explanation: Area of a circle is A = π*r². If radius becomes 2r, new area = π*(2r)² = 4πr² (increases by a factor of 4).

questions.question: If 5 workers can build a wall in 12 days, how many days will 10 workers take to build the same wall?
questions.explanation: Total Work = 5 workers * 12 days = 60 worker-days. Days for 10 workers = 60 / 10 = 6 days.

questions.question: What is the sum of interior angles in a hexagon (6-sided polygon)?
questions.explanation: Formula for interior angle sum = (n - 2) * 180°. For n=6: (6 - 2) * 180° = 4 * 180° = 720°.

quizzes.title: World General Knowledge & Trivia
quizzes.description: Challenge your awareness on world geography, notable history, famous landmarks, and international facts.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin on Earth, covering more than 30% of the Earth's total surface area.

questions.question: Who is known as the inventor of the World Wide Web (WWW)?
questions.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN in Switzerland.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen as the capital city of Australia in 1908 as a compromise between rival cities Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which country is home to the ancient Wonder of the World: The Great Pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Pyramids of Giza are located on the Giza plateau near Cairo, Egypt.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River in northeastern Africa is traditionally considered the longest river in the world, spanning approximately 6,650 km (4,132 miles).

questions.question: In what year did the Apollo 11 mission successfully land astronauts on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the Apollo 11 Lunar Module on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

questions.question: What is the hardest natural substance known on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond is the hardest naturally occurring mineral, scoring a 10 (maximum) on the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.question: Which continent is known as the 'Dark Continent' historically?
questions.explanation: Africa was historically referred to as the 'Dark Continent' by 19th-century Europeans due to its unexplored interior terrain.

questions.question: How many time zones are there in Russia?
questions.explanation: Spanning across Eastern Europe and Northern Asia, Russia currently spans 11 standard time zones (UTC+2 to UTC+12).

questions.question: Which currency is used in Japan?
questions.explanation: The Japanese Yen (¥ / JPY) is the official legal tender of Japan.

quizzes.title: English Grammar & Vocabulary
quizzes.description: Sharpen your verbal ability, identifying parts of speech, correct verb tenses, synonyms, and idiom usage.

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence with proper subject-verb agreement:
options: Neither of the boys were present yesterday.
Neither of the boys was present yesterday.
Neither of the boys are present yesterday.
Neither of the boys have been present yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is a singular indefinite pronoun and takes the singular past verb 'was'.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'BENEVOLENT'?
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning, kind-hearted, and generous (opposed to malevolent).

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'She has been studying in this college ____ 2021.'
questions.explanation: We use 'since' to denote a specific starting point in time (since 2021), whereas 'for' denotes a duration of time (for 3 years).

questions.question: What does the idiom 'Bite the bullet' mean?
options: To eat something hard and chewy
To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure a painful or unavoidable situation that one has been putting off.

questions.question: Which of the following is an antonym of 'OBSOLETE'?
questions.explanation: Obsolete means out of date or no longer produced/used. Its opposite is 'modern' or 'current'.

questions.question: Identify the part of speech of the capitalized word: 'She spoke ELOQUENTLY at the conference.'
questions.explanation: 'Eloquently' is an adverb because it modifies how the action was performed (spoke eloquently).

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Accommodation' with double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.question: Select the sentence in passive voice:
options: The chef prepared a wonderful meal.
A wonderful meal was prepared by the chef.
The chef is preparing a wonderful meal.
The chef will prepare a wonderful meal.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the object ('a wonderful meal') becomes the subject receiving the action performed by the agent ('by the chef').

questions.question: What is a group of lions called?
questions.explanation: A collective noun for a family or group of lions is a 'pride'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'If I ____ rich, I would travel around the world.'
questions.explanation: In second conditional statements expressing hypothetical/imaginary situations (subjunctive mood), 'were' is grammatically used for all subjects.
